## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] New `stopAgent` destructure breaks an existing dispatch test; CI test job is red — `src/lib/cloister/review-agent.ts:477`
- Severity: ! (MUST)
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect (in-PR test regression, validation gap); in_pr_scope.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: this PR changed the dynamic import in `spawnReviewRoleForIssueBody` to `const { spawnRun, saveAgentState, getAgentState, getLatestSessionId, resumeAgent, stopAgent, wipeAgentStateDirs } = await import('../agents.js');` (FR-8 / WI-3). The unchanged test `tests/unit/lib/cloister/guard-advancing-dispatch.test.ts` mocks `../../../../src/lib/agents.js` at line 16 without a `stopAgent` export. Vitest throws on the missing mock export at the destructure, the outer `try` catches it, and `spawnReviewRoleForIssue` returns a failure.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected `spawnRun('PAN-2420', 'review', …)` to be called; observed `[review-agent] Failed to spawn review role for PAN-2420: Error: [vitest] No "stopAgent" export is defined on the "../../../../src/lib/agents.js" mock` and `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 'PAN-2420', 'review', …(1) ]`. `test-shard (4/4)` and the aggregate `test` job fail on this exact head, so `verification.tests` is red and the PR cannot advance. Production is not affected: `src/lib/agents.ts:77` exports `stopAgent`.
- Evidence: `gh pr checks 4440` → `test fail`, `test-shard (4/4) fail` (run 36753497601, job 110017778981; log: `Test Files 1 failed | 435 passed (436)`). Reproduced locally: `npx vitest run tests/unit/lib/cloister/guard-advancing-dispatch.test.ts` → `Tests 1 failed | 5 passed (6)`, the same assertion at line 155. The test file is not in this PR's diff, so the failure comes from the changed import.
- Fix: add `stopAgent: vi.fn()` to the `agents.js` mock. The test's `resumeAgent` returns `{ success: false }` with no error, so the stop branch is never taken; the export only needs to exist for the destructure. Add it to the mock in `tests/unit/lib/cloister/guard-advancing-dispatch.test.ts`. Then grep the other `vi.mock(...agents.js...)` factories that reach `spawnReviewRoleForIssueBody` and add it wherever it is missing. Re-run the file and confirm the CI test job is green.

## Non-blocking Findings

### ~ [correctness] `runtimeWaitingOnHuman` guard is inert in the deacon child — `src/lib/cloister/silent-reviewer-recovery.ts:89`
- Classification: implementation defect, low impact; in_pr_scope (CodeRabbit raised the same point).
- `runDeaconLite` runs in the forked deacon child (`src/dashboard/server/deacon-main.ts`). `getAgentRuntimeStateSync` reads only the in-process runtime mirror, which `src/lib/agents/runtime-state.ts:99-103` documents as populated only inside the dashboard server. In the child it returns null, so this guard (D5 "Runtime mirror waiting-on-human → skip") never fires in production. The test injects the dep, so it passes.
- Impact is bounded. A reviewer that waits on a human has already received its prompt and written the tool call to its transcript, so `classifyReviewer` returns `active` and the routine does not act on it. Permission prompts on Herdr also surface as `backendState === 'blocked'`, which is guarded. I found no reachable path where a silent (transcript-less) reviewer is also waiting on a human.
- Suggested fix: use the async `getAgentRuntimeState` Effect, which falls back to the dashboard over HTTP outside the server process, and make the dep async. Alternatively, drop the guard and document why the transcript check subsumes it.

### ? [correctness] Lane re-dispatch can no-op after the lane was already reset — `src/lib/cloister/silent-reviewer-recovery.ts:111-116`
- Classification: unconfirmed hypothesis.
- `redispatchLane` closes the pane and removes the lane state directory, then calls `recoverMissingConvoyReviewers`. That function skips any lane whose `<subRole>.md` exists at all (`review-convoy.ts:434`, no mtime check), while the detector counts only a report written since the stamp (D4). If a lane was dispatched for a run that already held its report from an earlier dispatch, the door returns `success: true` ("no-op"). The routine then logs "re-dispatched", but nothing launches. Because the state dir is gone, no later tick can escalate it. I did not find a production path that dispatches a lane over an existing same-run report, because the convoy launch itself skips such lanes. A test with a pre-existing lane report plus an injected door that returns no-op would establish this. A cheap guard: treat a no-op result (`message` includes "no-op", or no lane was actually launched) as a failed re-dispatch and escalate it.

### Notes (no action required)
- FR-8 extension: the parent fallback also stops the agent when resume refused with "it appears healthy" (`resume.ts:211`). This is reasonable, because otherwise the fresh spawn would collide with a live parent.
- Performance: each 60s tick scans every agent `state.json` (sync, in the deacon child, not the dashboard event loop) and reads the pipeline journal once per stamped reviewer. States without `reviewDispatchedAt` exit before any I/O. This is bounded and not material at the current scale (268 active issues).

### Dimensions
- Correctness: one blocker (test regression), one bounded advisory (inert guard), one hypothesis. The core detection logic was traced against real inputs. For claude-code (the live review harness, `roles.review.model: workhorse:mid` → `claude-opus-5-5`), `getHeartbeat` resolves the transcript through the absolute path in `sessions.json` (PAN-3948), which works in the deacon child. I verified on this reviewer's own agent dir that the indexed path exists and its mtime advances live. So an active reviewer is not falsely flagged. Active-heartbeat files are older than 5 minutes, so the passive JSONL mtime governs. The re-dispatch runs inside `withReviewLifecycleGuard`, and `spawnReviewRoleForIssue` re-enters the same guard safely (AsyncLocalStorage held set). `review.redispatched` is never written (D6), and `stalledReviewReason` (`deacon-lite.ts:259-267`) matches only `review.dispatched`/`review.redispatched`/`review.requested`, so `recoverStalledReviews` ignores the new `review.stalled`/`review.stall-escalated` tails and cannot launch convoy lanes on a quick-mode issue.
- Security: no new trust boundary, no user-controlled input reaches a sensitive operation, and `removeAgentStateDir` keeps its containment checks. NFR-2 holds: the detection path reads the journal, state, report mtimes, transcript mtime, liveness, and local `git rev-parse` (`deriveReviewRunHead8`). The conflict gate on the re-dispatch door shows no gh/fetch in its deps.
- Performance: bounded; see the note above.
- Requirements/UX: all FRs are implemented. The needs-you surface goes through `surfaceIssueFeedbackNeedsYou` (D10). No stub UI. The new tests are in the default vitest include and ran in CI.
